_what: THE MEDICINE AS AN OPERATION (Air, after the first .695 production read, 2026-10-05): the record licenses the corrective operation; the Reader instantiates it inside the person's own problem. One line per signature, written by hand by True from the record's what-it-is + extended + the 78 hand-written acts (lib/pour/medicineActs.js), in ordinary words, operation-shaped, uninstantiated: no scenario, no time of day, no number of minutes, no other person unless the capacity is itself interpersonal. Merged into lib/data/plain_propositions.json as `medicine`.

medicine.0: Leave it undecided a while longer: meet the thing before you know what it is, and look at it without the name you have been giving it.
medicine.1: Choose this and not that, and mean it: point your attention at one thing and take the first step in that direction.
medicine.2: Go with what you already know before you reason about it: notice which part matters, begin with that part, and let the rest wait.
medicine.3: Tend the growing thing a little, today, and ask nothing of it yet: give it what it needs now, without steering it toward a result.
medicine.4: Give the mess a shape it can be carried in: one rule, a time, a place, or the order things go in; the smallest structure that holds it.
medicine.5: Hand one thing on the way it was handed to you, or join the practice other people keep; learn how it was done before you.
medicine.6: Be with the person in it without fixing it: feel it alongside them, keep your own side, and stay in contact while it is hard.
medicine.7: Move toward what you want, one step, today, in the direction you chose; keep going through the next bit of resistance.
medicine.8: Carry it without tightening around it: keep your shape under the weight, keep the thing its real size, and bear the next stretch without deciding anything.
medicine.9: Do the small practice again, alone, today, even when it feels pointless; repeat one piece of it until it improves.
medicine.10: Meet what is arriving as it arrives: notice what is newly here right now and receive it, instead of bracing for it or opening the door early.
medicine.11: Put it back in proportion: give back what is owed and take what is yours, adjust the share until it is fair, then stop keeping score.
medicine.12: Let go of the thing you are gripping, on purpose: put it down, leave your hands empty a while, and keep the act while giving up the outcome.
medicine.13: Let the thing end that is already over: close it, honour it, mark the ending with a plain act, and do not reopen it.
medicine.14: Adjust one thing a little and then stop: add or take away a small amount, feel the difference, and find the centre by small corrections, not a lurch.
medicine.15: Look at how it works underneath this one case: trace the pattern across the last few times, say the mechanism in one line, and change nothing yet.
medicine.16: Stop holding up the thing that cannot hold and let it come down; clear what fell, and stand in the gap without rebuilding yet.
medicine.17: Turn toward what you actually want: name it plainly to yourself, pick the one you would be sorriest to lose, and face it again.
medicine.18: Take the next step with only enough light for that step: picture how it could turn out well, keep the picture, and do not demand the whole road.
medicine.19: Do the thing in your own way without proving anything: let what you are show, stop performing it, and put your own name on what is already yours.
medicine.20: Look at the same thing longer until it shows you more: see the whole pattern you are standing inside, with yourself marked on it.
medicine.21: Finish the thing that has been waiting on its last step: close it, gather what it became, and leave the door open for what comes next.
medicine.22: Begin while it is still nothing in particular: catch the first spark, start without deciding what it is for, and let the impulse move before there is a plan.
medicine.23: Choose one direction because it is what you want, and go that way: stop surveying, decide from the wanting rather than the logic, and face one way for a while.
medicine.24: Say the shape of it out loud, in the open, before anyone asks: claim the structure as yours and state the order of things once, without arguing it.
medicine.25: Move at the pace your feeling can sustain: let what you want and what you will do go the same way, and keep a steady rhythm rather than a surge.
medicine.26: Let the hard part test what you are committed to: engage it on purpose, drop the approach that is not working, and keep the purpose.
medicine.27: Do the giving where it can be seen by the people it is for, this time, without a word about it; and accept the acknowledgment when it comes.
medicine.28: Defend the direction you chose against the next push: gather your determination, keep the heading when it is contested, and refuse the pull off course once more.
medicine.29: Decide it and act on it the same day, without explaining: let the decision act instead of announcing it, and carry it through.
medicine.30: Keep going toward what you chose after everything that has happened: carry on through another stretch of doubt without needing a sign.
medicine.31: Carry what you began all the way into form: bring the possibility to its full size and let what was only possible stand finished.
medicine.32: Look before you interpret: see the thing as if for the first time, describe what is in front of you in plain lines, and draw no conclusions yet.
medicine.33: Hold what you know a while before saying it: weigh it, keep two true things without declaring either, and write both sides down before you speak.
medicine.34: Work it through to what actually follows: cut through the story, count it out, read what the numbers or the facts show, and reason it from the start once.
medicine.35: Put the problem down and let your mind rest: stop adjusting for an hour, sit still until things settle, and rest in the balance you already have.
medicine.36: Sort what matters from what does not, carefully: strike one thing from the list that does not serve, and sharpen one skill by repeating its hardest part.
medicine.37: Show someone the way you found: walk the route with a person who is lost on it, give directions plainly once, and let them walk it.
medicine.38: Gather your scattered thoughts into one line: bring the two sides of your thinking into one plan, and sort the pieces into a shape you can act on.
medicine.39: Go all the way into it until you meet its edge: follow the thought past where it is comfortable, stay in the depth, and read the hardest part twice before stopping.
medicine.40: Let several things be true at once and act on one: sort the pulls on you from each other, and mark which of them are actually yours.
medicine.41: See the whole of it with nothing hidden: lay every piece out where you can see them at once, and look until there is nothing left to see.
medicine.42: Open before anything has arrived: let the feeling in without deciding what it is, and sit with nothing in your hands and let what comes, come.
medicine.43: Choose one connection and go with it: join the other person in the work so the two of you move as one, and meet them in the middle.
medicine.44: Share the good thing with the people it belongs to, on the day it happens: let the gladness go out to the room, and celebrate with them, not after them.
medicine.45: Sit with what your heart already knows: let the feeling settle, rest in the connection without doing anything with it, and spend time with what you love with no task attached.
medicine.46: Act on your private sense of what is right: do the fair thing where no one will see, and return the small thing you owe before anyone asks.
medicine.47: Give one thing and take one thing, in balance: accept what is offered for what you gave, return the favour at its true size, and let the exchange run both ways.
medicine.48: Let yourself be drawn before you choose: look at the feelings that might be felt, follow the pull a little way, and go once toward the thing that draws you to see it up close.
medicine.49: Walk toward what truly connects and leave what does not: go deeper into the shared thing than is comfortable, and leave the hollow ritual for the living one.
medicine.50: Let the satisfaction of a finished thing land: enjoy what you imagined now that it is here, use it for a while instead of improving it, and reach for nothing past it.
medicine.51: Feel the whole of it: name every feeling in it, none crossed out, and know the feeling fully before you move on.
medicine.52: Decide what this is for before you spend it: hold the first resource in your hand, say in one line what will be built, and name only that.
medicine.53: Tend what grows with a steady, responsible hand: balance the competing demands and keep tending, without clutching.
medicine.54: Build the first new thing on the cleared ground: make it small and skilled, with your own hands, where the false thing fell.
medicine.55: Keep what the change produced as it is: hold the new form steady instead of reopening it, protect what the ending won, and set the finished thing down in a form that keeps.
medicine.56: Keep going on your own reserves through the pressure: carry your own share, all of it, without checking on anyone else, and stand firm.
medicine.57: Share your strength where it is needed: give one concrete piece of help and finish it, and hold the other person up with what you have.
medicine.58: Gather what the change grew: count what the ending gave you, take in the yield, and collect the fruit of the patient wait.
medicine.59: Keep building with sustained craft: return to the work daily, do today's part of the long build, and deepen the mastery by persisting.
medicine.60: Enjoy what careful tending has grown: let the abundance be seen and used, take pleasure in the grown thing, and rest in the result.
medicine.61: Establish the thing that lasts: finish it by sustained will, and complete the form so it stands without you.
medicine.62: Start the thing for the spark of starting: explore a direction before it has a destination, and ask the beginner's question about where to go.
medicine.63: Cut through the inertia with one decisive act: set a boundary and hold it, charge forward on the decision you made, and lead the change by moving first.
medicine.64: Tend the fire without burning out: keep the motivation warm with steady care, feed the drive a little at a time, and hold the direction day after day.
medicine.65: Release what is done and keep what is not: bear the duty, drop one condition you set, take the step, and know what to let go of.
medicine.66: Listen as a student of it: ask the question you do not know the answer to, follow a raw curiosity, and look with fresh eyes before judging.
medicine.67: Reason it through fast and cleanly: cut to the logic, think it to its sharp point, plan the next three moves, and act on it.
medicine.68: Tell the truth with care for when and how: say the hard thing gently, once, in the form the other person can hear, and keep the clarity steady.
medicine.69: Write the facts down in order, without feeling words: apply the method once, rigorously, and judge it by the discipline, not the mood.
medicine.70: Sense what has not happened yet, with wonder: envision it freshly, feel toward it with fresh sensitivity, dream the next step and take it.
medicine.71: Pursue the emotional truth with someone, in the open: make a ritual of the shared thing, and teach what you feel by doing it with others.
medicine.72: Make room for what the other person feels without fixing it: ask how it feels to them, stay with the answer, and keep the connection while it is hard without drowning in it.
medicine.73: Make the fair call about a feeling, yourself: judge the hurt fairly after it has finished, by principle rather than reaction, and weigh what it costs them against what it gives.
medicine.74: Learn how the thing grows by tending it: apprentice yourself to it, care for it with fresh hands, and see what it needs.
medicine.75: Force the change into reality by steady effort: move the structure one real inch, slowly and without stopping, and build the change by persistent work.
medicine.76: Release what is done and keep what serves: clear what is finished so the rest can grow, and keep the material thing sustainable.
medicine.77: Build the thing that endures: hold the weight as a builder holds stone, and lay the one step you can see, solidly.

mechanism.1: This is an invitation, not a fix: what this working part of you could feed next, if you want it to.
mechanism.2: The way through is to do what this other capacity does. It is the opposite kind of thing from what you are doing too much of.
mechanism.3: The way through is not to push harder at the thing you are doing too little of. It is to do this other capacity's own action; doing that is what brings the first one back.
mechanism.4: The way through is a simpler, earlier version of the same thing you are already doing, done as your own.
